p: The "Beisl" is very popular amongst local Viennese.
Opened in 1900, the café has historic decor with old tables and mirrors. It is situated in front of the main railway station Westbahnhof, which makes it practical to wait here for upcoming trains.
A traditional Viennese cafe that is very popular due to its central location on Mariahilfer Strasse.

The young architect Manfred Wuits together with the cook Zeljko Jovanovic transformed the previous tool hall/shop to an innovative popular bohemian bar. In summer time one can sit outside. There is free Wi-Fi. Usually on Sundays they…
It serves upper Austrian monastery beer Schlägl and must ("Most").
Tiny little artsy bar, smoking permitted.
The bar permits smoking and offers wines and vegan snacks.
A Chinese/Asian restaurant that gets consistent excellent gourmet reviews.
The Portuguese restaurant offers Bacalhao, Pastel de Nata and many different Portuguese wines.
A nice family-run Greek restaurant, with a good variety of items to choose from.
Pizza with just enough and not too many toppings, and very Italian selection. Austrian ingredients, when used, are unusual specialties.

Joseph Haydn spent the final twelve years of his life in this home, during which time he composed the oratorios The Creation and The Seasons. The house has been a museum since 1899, and careful restoration has included the small garden,…

On one side of the 2nd Worldwar bunker there are routes to climb high up until its roof with great views into the roofs of Vienna. The routes are usually hard and require some endurance. The alpine club organises courses for beginners…
A Cineplexx theater with plenty of choices including original versions. The cinema opened here in 1905. According to seat numbers it is one of the biggest in Vienna.
The theatre projects mostly English films in original version.
The restaurant inside the lesbian and queer "Rosa Lilla Villa" serves good international food.

The smallest Japanese restaurant in town. All the dishes are homemade, and the owners claim that they pay attention to a proper balance of ingredients – being full can also be healthy. The place is so small that there is no toilet…

The Salzberg restaurant serves Pongauer Kasnocken, made with special smoked cheese (Räucherkäse) from Salzburg province. There is a large selection of breakfast/brunch choices. The open air patio is on a quiet street.
Small coffee place nicely lost in the middle of Mariahilf. In winter the rustic and warm oven is wonderful. In summer one can sit outdoors.
Big selection of fine and rare bottles.
The bar serves good wine, with a popular dance floor (unusual in Vienna). Well-liked by women.

Houses the largest furniture collection in the world. The exhibit displays furniture for all the Austrian emperors since Charles VI (the father of Maria Theresa), furniture by the Thonet Brothers, Jugendstil, and the Viennese Modernist…
A trendy hang out place with its own unique vibe, in the area of the city frequented by art students. It is famous for its falafel.
This longstanding bar was legendary during the 1980s and 90s. It serves breakfast with many vegetarian options, as well as special beer from Vorarlberg.

The café is often bursting at the seams, but good tunes and decent service prevail. Good people watching and decor. One of Vienna's most popular meeting points. The bar serves warm food til late hours.
Built by the architects Ferdinand Fellner und Hermann Helmer in 1884/85.
It was built to thank for the access to the fresh water pipeline going to the central imperial palace for Margareten in 1835/36. It features Saint Margarete killing a dragon.
This very stylish cinema screens carefully chosen films.

This traditional Vienna restaurant offers good seasonal food and beer choices. The restaurant is non-smoking. Each room is specifically decorated, one of them is a traditional Zirben-Stube. The prices are fair and the portions big.
Chef Nikolai Kölbl serves enchanting versions of Viennese food. There are vegetarian options and the salads are good.

A modern interpretation of traditional Viennese food like Tafelspitzsulz, Blunzentascherln, Zwiebelrostbraten, and Kalbsrahmgulasch. It is particularly popular for its casual atmosphere and tasty, delicate food.
The "Gasthaus" serves Viennese food and Hackl Bräu (workers' beer).
The café serves breakfast, later cocktails and burgers, beware that people are heavily smoking.

The Rüdigerhof is a typical Viennese café, hence expect rude waiters (treat them with humor) and have enough time to chill out. It offers nice seats outdoor under trees next to the Vienna river. Indoor can be very smoky.
It is a bar, a restaurant, a gallery and a concert location. The bar serves good wines and cocktails. It is a location for smokers.
